q: Carathéodory's theorem extends the Riemann mapping φ: 𝔻 → U to the boundary when:
opts: U is a Jordan domain (bounded by a Jordan curve), in which case φ extends to a homeomorphism 𝔻̄ → Ū
U has finitely many boundary components
exp: Carathéodory extension theorem: if U is a Jordan domain, the Riemann map φ: 𝔻 → U extends continuously to a homeomorphism of the closed disk 𝔻̄ → Ū. This fails for domains with fractal boundaries (e.g., the complement of a Julia set may not be a Jordan domain).
